Your account and device data live only in your own Firebase project. Being paired never means permanent access — every session asks again.

Family Remote Support helps trusted people help each other with phones. This policy explains the data the app uses.

What is collected and stored
• Your account: name, email and Google account id used to sign in.
• Your device: model, manufacturer, Android version and app version, plus an app-scoped device id.
• Push token: used to deliver support-request notifications to your phone.
• Session records: who requested help, start/end time and final status.
• Live location: when you enable sharing, your latest location and related accuracy/time details are shared with the paired members you choose.
• Journey history and movement details: depending on the tracking features you use, location points may be saved as journey history with timestamps and available details such as accuracy, speed, bearing or altitude. Movement insights are derived from available location data.
• Saved places: place names, coordinates, alert radius and arrival/departure preferences may be saved in your Firebase project and mirrored in local app storage so alerts can work offline.

Screen and support data
• Screen sharing starts only for a support session you approve. The app does not intentionally collect passwords or keyboard contents as a data record. Do not type sensitive information while sharing your screen.

Where your data lives
Account, pairing, session and location-feature data may be stored in this app's Firebase project. Saved-place details are also cached on this device for offline alerts. Data is not sold to advertisers.

Who can see what
Access depends on the pairing, sharing settings and the app's access rules. Paired members may see location information made available by your enabled sharing/tracking features. Stop location sharing when you no longer want to share. Signing out stops this phone's location sharing and clears its local saved-place cache and notification log; it does not necessarily erase previously stored server-side history.

You stay in control: approve each support session, use location features only when you want them, review the available sharing controls, and stop sharing when finished.

These rules keep Family Remote Support safe for everyone.

1. Consent first. Every single help session needs a fresh, explicit approval on the phone that receives help. Pairing alone never grants access.

2. Pairing codes are one-time and expire in about 5 minutes. A code can be redeemed only once and only by the person who scans or types it in time.

3. Guest help is temporary. A guest connection expires by itself after 2 hours and can never become a permanent family pairing by itself.

4. You can always stop. The person being helped can deny a request, end a running session at any second, or revoke a paired phone completely.

5. The helper must be trusted. Only share your code or QR with people you actually trust. A helper sees your screen while a session runs — close sensitive apps first if you are unsure.

6. No bypassing. The app never tries to unlock a phone, read passwords, silently grant permissions, or hide that a session is running. It only works inside what Android explicitly allows.

7. Fair use only. Do not use the app to harass, spy on, or pressure anyone. Abuse leads to revoked access.

8. Families first. This app is built for helping family members and close friends with their phones — nothing else.

How to turn on Remote assist
Follow the 3 steps below exactly — you only ever need to do this once:
In Settings, find the \"Family Remote Support assist\" row in the list (our app\'s row — it is usually highlighted).
Tap the row and turn the switch ON.
When the Android warning appears, tap Allow.
⚠️ Careful: turning on \"Accessibility menu shortcut\" or any other switch will not work — that one is not ours! Only the \"Family Remote Support assist\" row is correct.
